question.problem:
The following table shows the water flow rate, $R(t),$ through a pipe (in liters per minute) over a period of $40$ minutes.

| $t\,\text{(minutes)}$ | $0$ | $10$ | $20$ | $30$ | $40$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $R\,\text{(liters/minute)}$ | $12$ | $15$ | $17$ | $16$ | $14$ |

Use the right Riemann sum for $R(t)$ over the interval $[0,40]$ with four subintervals to approximate the total volume of water pumped.

The total volume is 
{{field-1}} liters.

current_example.problem: Estimate the area under the curve $y=(2x-4)^2+2$ over the interval $[0,2]$ using a right Riemann sum with step size $\Delta x=0.5.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's sketch our situation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14222967/assets/94618262fb303035cd03ccf0274694d7083d9cd3a23d4231e3a8fccde8ac4fe1.png)

 

The area $\mathcal{A}$ can be approximated using the formula

$$
\mathcal A\approx(\overbrace{{\color{red}{f(0.5)}}+{\color{red}{f(1)}}+{\color{red}{f(1.5)}}+{\color{red}{f(2)}}}^{\color{red}{\large\text{heights}}})\cdot \underbrace{\color{blue}\Delta x}_{\color{blue}{\large\text{width}}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $f(x)$ at each point:

| $x$ | $0.5$ | $1$ | $1.5$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $11$ | $6$ | $3$ | $2$ |

Finally, we obtain the following approximation for our area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(11+6+3+2)\cdot 0.5 \\  & =22\cdot 0.5 \\  & =11\end{aligned}
$$
